messages:
sara: FYI the release pipeline is stuck on the regenerate check for 1.13.0. CI shows diffs but we didn't touch API shapes.
sara: publish blocked by release-bot: "regen diff detected". I'm seeing changes in `packages/sdk/auth.ts` and `packages/sdk/types/index.ts`.
devin: can you paste the diff?
sara: 
```
$ git --no-pager diff packages/sdk/auth.ts
diff --git a/packages/sdk/auth.ts b/packages/sdk/auth.ts
index 9a1b2c3..b7c8d9e 100644
--- a/packages/sdk/auth.ts
+++ b/packages/sdk/auth.ts
@@ -22,7 +22,7 @@ export interface RetryOptions {
-  maxAttempts?: number;
-  backoff?: number;
+  backoff?: number;
+  maxAttempts?: number;
}
```
lin: order swapped again. looks like codegen emits optional fields in insertion order based on map iteration. this inconsistent ordering triggers typegen diffs.
devin: that should be cosmetic but semantic-release interprets any changes in `packages/sdk` as a new minor. we've had noise in changelogs for these non-functional reorders.
sara: release-bot said: "blocked: regenerated files differ from committed files. Please commit regenerated files or add [skip-release] to bypass."
devin: skipping releases is bad. we risk shipping desynced code. fix options: pin codegen binary, make codegen deterministic, or add a post-write normalization step.
lin: quick fix: add a normalization pass that sorts object keys and optional members alphabetically before emitting. also add deterministic glob sort for file traversal.
sara: I pushed a branch with a stable-write util and a CI job that runs `make regen` twice and fails if there's a diff. see PR #842.
devin: nice. also we should add a tiny unit test for the auth shape so future ordering won't slip.
lin: longer-term: we should update the release policy so that pure ordering-only diffs are classified as patch. semantic-release has plugins to override commit-types; we could add a detection hook to auto-label the release.
sara: note: we had a developer who relied on enum iteration order in a sample app; the sample passed locally but broke for one customer after publish. that's why I'd prefer not to silence these diffs without extra guards.
devin: agreed. add a smoke test in the release job that installs the freshly built SDK into example/sample-app and runs its integration test. if that catches behavior regressions, then order-only changes that don't affect sample apps are probably safe.
lin: CI patch: add `regen-twice` step and `smoke-sample` step before `semantic-release`. I updated .github/workflows/release.yml in the branch.
sara: CI run on branch shows regen-twice failed initially but after stable-write it passed. smoke-sample also passed.
ci-bot: build #3510: regen-twice passed, smoke-sample passed.
release-bot: release blocked previously; now queued. semantic-release still proposes v1.13.0 because it saw "chore: regen" commits.
devin: we should commit a changelog entry explicitly describing the non-functional regen fix and mark as patch. I'll add a `chore: regen (non-functional) [patch]` commit type that our release script treats as patch.
lin: let's also add CONTRIBUTING note: run `make regen && git diff --quiet || (echo 'regen changed files, commit them' && exit 1)` as pre-merge step.
sara: created ISSUE: https://redwood-internal/issue/5240 - "classify non-functional regen diffs as patch and add double-regen CI check". linking PRs for stable-write and release script tweak.
devin: thank you. once merged, let's monitor the weekly releases for noise reduction.
sara: merging now. will monitor sample apps and customer reports.
release-bot: published @redwood/sdk v1.13.0 (patch override) - success.
sara: closing thread. please reopen if you see any more publish hiccups.
lin: thanks all.
